messages:
alex: Quick sync — need to finalize Q2 runtime perf priorities. tradeoffs: kernels vs quant vs kv cache. customer asks from Finance and Platform teams are pushing for lower p95 at 2k tokens.

marta: Agree. We also have Dedicated customers asking for deterministic tail latency.

jin: Proposal: prioritize KV cache + small kernel improvements first (low risk, quick wins), then medium-term opt: kernel refactor + quant pipeline.

sam: Can you list concrete launch criteria? execs want measurable gates.

alex: Draft launch criteria: p95 latency reduction >=20% at 2k tokens on xlarge models; throughput improvement >=1.5x under 80% load for batch sizes we expect; end-to-end mem usage down 30% for quant path; no >2% regression on our eval suite (safe prompts).

caroline: Customers also asked for canary and fallback plan: if quantized path degrades, auto-fallback to float-16 with throttling. Need runbook.

infra-bot: perf-metrics: latest cluster run -> p50 90ms, p95 420ms at 2k tokens, throughput 11 req/s per GPU. (reported 1772034500)

marta: That p95 is rough. KV cache should help majority of sessions with repeated prompts. Estimate: KV reduces token work by ~35% for conversational workloads.

jin: Rough roadmap sketch: Phase 0 (2 weeks): telemetry + benchmarks per model family; Phase 1 (6 weeks): KV cache improvements + cheap kernel tweaks; Phase 2 (8-10 weeks): quantization pipeline + kernel refactor; Phase 3 (4 weeks): rollout, canary, payoffs & docs.

alex: Need to map to OKRs. Proposed OKR: Reduce inference cost per 1k tokens by 25% and p95 latency by 30% for long-context use cases by end of Q2. KR examples: KV hit rate >=40% for chat workloads; quantized path adopted for 30% of volume without eval regression >2%; canary rollback rate <1%.

sam: Dependencies: model-ops for quant pipelines, eng-platform for canary infra, docs + support. Any blockers?

caroline: Support will need a short FAQ and a troubleshooting checklist for weird hallucinations when switching quant models. Also legal for private deployments re: KMS.

marta: We should prioritize by impact vs risk. Quick table in thread:
- KV cache improvements: impact medium-high, risk low, cost dev 2 dev-weeks
- Kernel micro-ops (small hotfixes): impact medium, risk low-med, cost 3 dev-weeks
- Quant pipeline end-to-end: impact high, risk med-high, cost 8-10 dev-weeks
- Kernel refactor (large): impact high, risk high, cost 12+ dev-weeks

jin: So recommend MVP = KV + micro kernel + canary infra. Defer heavy refactor to next quarter unless customers pay.

alex: Sounds reasonable. Action items:
- @marta add detailed benchmark plan + datasets (due: 1772100000).
- @jin scope quant pipeline end-to-end and list infra needs (due: 1772150000).
- @sam own rollout/canary policy & runbook (due: 1772140000).
- @caroline draft customer comms & support FAQ (due: 1772130000).

caroline: I'll draft comms. Quick question: what is our rollback SLA?

sam: Rollback target: detect regressions within 30m of canary start, full rollback within 2 hours for prod. Playbook in runbook.

marta: We should also define monitoring signals: model quality regression (eval delta), p95 tail, KV hit ratio, OOMs, error-rate. If quality delta > 1.5% or p95 increase >10% in canary -> auto-hold.

alex: Good. One more governance ask: any change touching kernel refactor needs design doc + perf baseline + two reviewers from eng-runtime + eng-infra.

jin: I'll start the design doc for quant pipeline with benchmarks attached.

infra-bot: scheduled: perf-benchmark job queued at 1772035000.

alex: ok, thanks all. We'll include this in product roadmap sync tomorrow. If no objections by EOD we'll lock MVP scope: KV + micro kernel fixes + canary infra + quant scoping. React with :thumbsup: to agree, :eyes: to follow.

marta: :thumbsup:

jin: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

caroline: :eyes:
